title: Plugin hooks: say what the session needs, send nothing when nothing is pending, never repeat
description: Guy, 2026-10-13 via sock-client, from his phone: 'These messages are not helpful. Is something waiting on me, then tell me what I need to do in the sock message.' Today idle_prompt and Stop post fixed phrases ('<project>: waiting for you', 'finished a turn') through notify.sh. Wanted: when a session is waiting on him, the message carries the ask from the session's last assistant message (hook input last_assistant_message for Stop; the transcript tail for idle_prompt), trimmed to the question or decision, capped, code blocks dropped; when nothing is pending, nothing is sent (the notify_on_stop opt-in keeps 'finished a turn' for those who want it); the same pending ask is not reposted (hash of the ask kept per project in the state dir). permission_prompt forwards the Notification message, which names the tool. This reverses the v1 'fixed phrase, never transcript text' decision at the owner's request; the spec records why. Tests first in test/notify_test.go.
close_reason: Shipped 9e8a549 (plugin 0.2.0) and the security-review fixes in 3ae4e73: per-turn dedupe, no hash tool skips dedupe, token and secret-shape redaction, other fence shapes, text on stdin, regular-file and 2 MiB transcript fallback skipping tool-only entries. Not taken: an (agent) marker on the prefix, UTF-8-safe cut (valid in tests), double send under concurrent idle.

title: Claude plugin: several sessions on one machine share one puppet and compete for its deliveries
description: Seen 2026-10-13: the plugin is user-scoped, so every Claude Code session on the Mac runs sock-mcp --channel as the same puppet (MacM5Claude). A puppet token is one device with one delivery stream, so sessions compete for the owner's replies; the orchestrator session and this one both received or lost replies. The v1 assumption 'one puppet per machine' breaks for anyone running more than one session. Options: (a) per-session device tokens minted at sock-mcp startup (needs a minting capability the plugin token lacks: a sock-mcp or hub change), (b) hub-side fan-out to every connected device of a puppet (Messaging change, deliveries per device already exist), (c) a single-consumer election on the machine (lock file) so only one session's channel subscribes and the others are outbound-only, with the session that holds it named in sock_whoami. (c) is local and shippable now; (a) or (b) is the real fix. Decide with the hub team; spec first.
notes: Shipped: hook machine-key path (plugin 0.3.2), sock-cli v0.2.2 puppets ensure, sock-mcp v0.2.3 Codex fallback. Closes after yje live check: Guy runs sock machine-key create, sets the plugin key, two repos give two puppets.

title: sock-mcp change: Claude Code channel is lost when the 2026-07-28 revision is negotiated
description: Corrected diagnosis (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#push-messages-with-channels, changelog 2.1.292 and 2.1.295): on Claude Code's v2 runtime a channel server that negotiates revision 2026-07-28 is NOT registered as a channel; a server on the earlier handshake is. Since 2.1.292 local stdio servers negotiate 2026-07-28 by default (MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy opts out). sock-mcp on go-sdk v1.8.0 accepts the new handshake, so Claude Code 2.1.296 lands on 2026-07-28 and shows: Channel messages from plugin:sock:sock are unavailable: this connection's protocol version has no channel delivery path for claude. Live-seen 2026-10-13 with puppet MacM5Claude; tools work, inbound does not. Workaround for users now: MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy in the environment of claude. Fix in sock/mcp: when --channel is set, offer protocol versions only up to 2025-11-25 so Claude Code falls back to the legacy handshake and registers the channel (find the go-sdk option or hook for the supported-version list); lift the cap when Claude Code's changelog adds channel delivery on 2026-07-28. Document the env workaround in claude-code/README.md meanwhile. Verify with an owner reply arriving as a channel tag.
